title: Monica's dream (3.11)
hook: she dreams she and her son stand on the same wooden rule
tomorrow: who was the friend he called half of his soul?

segments.voice: A week of Augustine's early pages: come in, it starts early, weeping for dido, not alone, carthage. And yesterday, a book that set him longing for wisdom, with one name missing. Behind all of it, someone was praying.
screen: `LONGING FOR WISDOM.` → `A WEEK OF EARLY PAGES.`

segments.voice: A porch light left on all night for someone who isn't home yet. Augustine's mother, Monica, waited like that. And what did she see in her dream? She was standing on a wooden rule, a long straight edge, grieving. A bright young man came toward her, cheerful, and asked why she was sad.
screen: `THE PORCH LIGHT LEFT ON.` → `MONICA ON A WOODEN RULE.` → `WHY ARE YOU SAD?`

segments.voice: She told him she was mourning her son's ruin. He told her to look, and see that where she was, there her son was too. She looked, and there was Augustine, beside her on the same rule. When she told him the dream, he tried a clever reading: maybe it meant she'd come over to where he was. She answered at once. No. It wasn't said where he is, you are too. It was said where you are, he is too. Augustine writes that her quick answer moved him more than the dream itself. Here's the detail to keep. Monica doesn't step off her rule to stand where her son is. She stays, and in the dream he's brought to her. And Augustine is honest that it didn't happen soon. Years went by, he says, while he stayed in the mud and she kept praying. So this whole week, the narrow room, the nursery, Dido, the pear tree, Carthage, the book on fire, was lived while someone stood on a rule, praying for him.
screen: `WHERE YOU ARE, HE IS TOO.` · `HIS CLEVER READING. HER NO.` · `SHE STAYS ON THE RULE.` · `YEARS, NOT DAYS.` · then, large: `THE SAME RULE.`

segments.voice: Send one short message to someone who feels far off, in faith, in hope or just in distance, a line that asks for nothing back. Then put the phone down and stay where you are with their name, the way Monica stayed on her rule. Catholics who pray might ask God, quietly, to bring that person to stand beside them.
Monica's dream. A mother on a wooden rule, told that where she stands, her son will stand too.
Here's your line: the same rule, kept by someone who waited instead of chasing. A week of Augustine, done.
